newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo 1997 exports to rise up to 48 pct - report.
newsitem.headline: Yugo 1997 exports to rise up to 48 pct - report.

text.p: Yugoslavia expects exports to rise as much as 48 percent in 1997, the Yugoslav chamber of commerce reported on Wednesday.
The government estimates exports will rise 44.4 to 48.2 percent in 1997 and imports 17.3 to 20.4 percent, the chamber of commerce said in a report.
But previous government forecasts for high export growth have proved unrealistic, independent economists said.
Yugoslavia estimated a 50-percent rise in exports this year but instead, recorded a trade deficit of $1.7 billion in the first ten months of the year.
Cumulative January-October exports came to $1.4 billion and imports to $3.1 billion.

The proposed economic programme for 1997 should secure 10-13 percent growth in gross domestic product (GDP), a rise in industrial production between 10.8-13.9 percent and an expansion of agricultural production of five to six percent, the report said.
It said the estimated share of public spending in GDP should be between 46.6 to 48 percent.
Real wages and pensions are forecast to rise nine percent, according to the report. -- Gordana Kukic, Belgrade Newsroom ++381 11 222 4254
